events.did: met Mitch after nearly three years and told him he looked like shit
events.quote_anchor: VICTOR hadn’t seen Mitch in nearly three years, and the first thing he said was “You look like shit.”

events.did: twitched his fingers to turn the invisible dial all the way down, melting the strain out of Mitch’s body
events.quote_anchor: Victor’s fingers gave an incremental twitch, turning the invisible dial all the way down, and the strain melted out of Mitch’s body.

events.did: straightened up and punched Victor in the face
events.quote_anchor: He straightened, rolling the tension from his shoulders. And then he punched Victor in the face.

events.did: stopped Mitch’s fist by reaching for the current animating Mitch’s body like a web of strings and pulling
events.quote_anchor: Hadn’t reached for the current animating Mitch’s body like a web of strings and pulled.

events.did: shot the EON agent in the head when the agent rounded the van a second time
events.quote_anchor: The agent stopped moving long enough for Victor to shoot them in the head. This time, there was no getting up.

events.did: crossed to the dead body and freed the second comm
events.quote_anchor: Victor crossed to the dead body, and freed the second comm.

events.did: pressed the comm and a night vision scope into Mitch’s chest and pointed up at the ride overhead
events.quote_anchor: He pressed the comm and a night vision scope into Mitch’s chest, then pointed up, at a ride that loomed and coiled overhead.

events.did: ordered Mitch to get up onto the ride, be his eyes, and stay out of his way
events.quote_anchor: Get up there. Be my eyes. And stay out of my way.

relations.did: was Victor’s cellmate in the years they spent at Wrighton, where he never raised his voice nor protested Victor’s plans
relations.quote_anchor: Mitch, who in the years they’d spent at Wrighton, had never raised his voice. Never so much as protested one of Victor’s plans.

relations.did: would not leave the dog behind, as would neither Mitch
relations.quote_anchor: neither of whom would leave the dog behind

relations.did: insisted he could still help even though he was only an ordinary human
relations.quote_anchor: Mitch glared at him. “Being ordinary doesn’t make me powerless. I can still help.”

relations.did: was supposed to call Victor but never did
relations.quote_anchor: “You were supposed to call.” Victor frowned. “You didn’t.”
